recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-14166 unless BRR opens a new issue to redefine the current ResearchStudyPartyRole sponsor code or associatedParty guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-14166 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 BRR change request to change the ResearchStudy.sponsor definition, with Jira resolution noting that the change was made and published in the Dec 2017 FHIR ballot.
initial_application: Commit 61b5fa5576 explicitly listed GF#14166 and changed the old ResearchStudy spreadsheet's sponsor definition from a generic responsible organization to an organization that initiates the investigation and is legally responsible for the study. The researcher-overseeing-study wording in the seed snapshot appears on ResearchStudy.principalInvestigator in the same commit under sibling issue GF#14168.
additional_context: Later Published/Persuasive issue FHIR-37814 deleted ResearchStudy.sponsor, ResearchStudy.principalInvestigator, and ResearchStudy.contact for R5, representing sponsor and primary-investigator through ResearchStudy.associatedParty.role instead. Current source/fhir.ini maps ResearchStudy.sponsor to ResearchStudy.associatedParty.party with role='sponsor', current ResearchStudy source has no ResearchStudy.sponsor element, and BRR 2022-07-26 minutes record the 11-0-0 deletion motion. FHIR-37814 is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reintroducing or redefining ResearchStudy.sponsor would conflict with the later current-model decision, and changing the current sponsor role terminology to the old Jira wording is not supported by the FHIR-14166 scope.

related_jiras.note: Sibling ResearchStudy definition issue applied in the same 2017 commit; it explains the researcher-overseeing-study wording overlap in the FHIR-14166 snapshot.
Later Published BRR decision removed ResearchStudy.sponsor and moved sponsor representation to associatedParty.role; it is already represented on the combined branch.
